goal: Keep image and video generation behind a structured SOP brief so media tools consume reviewed prompts and all Feishu cards remain on the shared runtime gateway.

acceptance_criteria.description: Router metadata marks copy plus image/video requests as mixed content and records material status.
Harness content SOP validation fails when generated results omit image prompt, video script, source citations, or review checklist.
Feishu media generation cards continue to pass the card runtime gateway health gate.
Media generation produces a structured record with rollback hint, engine, status, structured prompt, and output reference.
LLM router, GPT Image, and Dreamina runtime paths finalize with media_generation cards and media generation records.

Chinese marketing poster/image requests keep GPT Image 2 as the primary provider through the media_sop provider prompt compiler registry, versioned prompt module library, and composable prompt recipe library, compile an English automotive marketing visual prompt for Image 2, preserve Chinese brand/text tokens verbatim, include brand asset, vehicle model, color, trim, and VI guardrails, accept source-grounded brand visual profiles, and use Dreamina as fallback or explicit opt-in.

acceptance_criteria.description: Low-friction prompt catalog presets follow the user-provided reference direction first, expose automotive WeChat cover, Rednote cover, festival poster, and launch key visual options so employees can choose outcomes without manually writing long prompts, and keep internal proposal changes behind feedback.

Source image edit requests such as background removal or cutout with an attached image must not be routed to text-to-image generation and should return a transparent PNG when a processable image is attached.

GPT Image, legacy Dreamina, and primary router success paths keep completed image result cards visible and deliver generated images as standalone interactive Feishu preview cards in the exact card conversation; preview-card upload or sending failures fall back to native image delivery and then the original session. Successful video result cards also remain visible so their Feishu sidebar H5 player stays reopenable.

Successful router video cards open a branded, responsive white-interface H5 player in Feishu sidebar-semi mode with custom playback, seek, volume, speed, picture-in-picture, fullscreen, close, loading, and failure states; the H5 endpoint accepts only bounded HTTP(S) media URLs, and a successfully finalized sidebar card suppresses the duplicate native video message while retaining native delivery as a card-failure fallback.
Session cancellation stops active media workers, removes persisted recovery records, and finalizes waiting cards as cancelled.
